critiques.area: Home tab and social surfaces: Home feed (src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx), Today's pours row (src/components/home/TodaysPours.tsx, groupPours.ts), feed post (src/components/PostCard.tsx), Activity (src/app/activity.tsx), single post (src/app/post/[id].tsx), pours viewer (src/app/pours/[authorId].tsx), and the chrome: src/components/FloatingTabBar.tsx and src/components/ScreenTopBar.tsx. Repo /Users/janmcqueeny/Projects/drinkdex-worktrees/polish, branch perf-fixes (build 13). Read-only critique, no files edited. Geometry below is reconstructed for an iPhone 17 Pro Max: 440x956pt, about 62pt safe top and 34pt safe bottom.

screens.name: Home feed (screen composition)
screens.what_it_looks_like_now: Cream #F7F2EA ground (index.tsx:267) with 3.5% paper grain laid over everything, the photos included, because Grain is mounted above the Stack (_layout.tsx:271). The top bar is the same cream (ScreenTopBar.tsx:257) and 44pt tall under the 62pt safe area, so it ends at about y=107. In it: a 26pt ink + glyph on the left, Playfair Bold 28/34 'Sipply' in wine centred (index.tsx:196-201, theme.ts:346), and a 26pt ink heart with a 6pt wine dot on the right. Its 1pt rule shows only once the list has scrolled past 1pt. Below it is the Today's pours row, about 136pt tall on the same cream, ending near y=243 with a hairline under it. Then post 1: a 56pt author row (to y=299), then a full-bleed 3:4 photo 440x587 (to y=886). The floating white tab bar starts near y=855, so at rest it covers the bottom ~31pt of the first photo and the whole of post 1's action row (y=886-930). The first screen is therefore cream bar, cream row, one photo cut off by a white slab, and no like control in view. Scrolling down, every cell is the same PostCard, roughly 760pt tall, with only 16pt of cream between one and the next. Loading shows a centred wine spinner under the row. An empty feed shows the shared EmptyState: a 36pt 'users' glyph, 'Nothing poured yet' at 22pt SemiBold, 16pt muted body, and a 200pt-wide filled wine 'Find friends' button. Pull to refresh shows the stock grey iOS spinner. The list simply stops at bottom padding, with no footer.
bland_problems: One continuous cream field from the status bar to the tab bar. The screen (index.tsx:267), the bar (ScreenTopBar.tsx:257) and the Today's row (TodaysPours.tsx:296-299, hairline only) share one ground, and the same `backgroundColor: colors.bg` is set in 19 route files under src/app. Home has no second ground and no band. The only brand object is the 28pt wordmark (index.tsx:196-201).
The feed is one stream of identical PostCard cells (index.tsx:123-136, 206-210). Nothing is interleaved, grouped or summarised, so twenty posts are twenty copies of the same 56/587/44/text cadence.
The first viewport ends badly. With TAB_BAR_CLEARANCE 84 (FloatingTabBar.tsx:55) and a 136pt Today's row, the white bar lands across the bottom of post 1's photo and hides its heart, share and save.

Pull to refresh uses the default RefreshControl, because only `refreshing`/`onRefresh` are passed (index.tsx:256-257). The most repeated gesture on Home draws a grey system spinner, while Reels tints its own (reels.tsx:157, tintColor reelInk).

The empty state of every new account is the generic EmptyState template (index.tsx:248-253, ui.tsx:1984-2030: glyph, 22pt title, 16pt body, button), the same one Activity, Post and the viewer use. 'Find friends' also appears twice on that screen: as a tile in the Today's row (TodaysPours.tsx:173-175) and as the wine button.
There is no ListFooterComponent (index.tsx:206-259). The feed ends in bare padding with nothing to close it.

None of the 162 catalog photographs appears anywhere on Home, even for a new user with nothing to show, which is the case that needs imagery most. src/data/drinkPhotos.ts is imported by the Dex, the drink page, log, stats and the celebration, but by no file in this area.
opportunities: Give Home's head its own ground. Put the top bar and Today's pours on a wineDeep #3E0A12 'back bar' band: wordmark in bone (textOnWine is about 13:1 there), tile frames bone at 2pt for unseen and wineSoft at 1pt for seen (about 3.4:1, enough for a non-text edge), labels in textOnWine, and a light status bar while at the top. The feed stays cream below. This keeps Instagram's structure (bar, row, posts) and gives the screen a focal point and a speakeasy door. ScreenTopBar needs a `tone` prop, and check-contrast needs the new pairs.

A scroll-linked wordmark that condenses as the feed moves, scale 1 to 0.8 via useAnimatedScrollHandler plus interpolate, with the full-size wordmark as its resting state. If Reanimated stalls, the brand simply stays big, so nothing can be hidden.

Interleave real-data modules every ~6 posts, the way Instagram interleaves suggestions, so the cadence breaks without borrowing its identity. For example, 'Not in your Dex yet': a horizontal strip of 2:3 cards for drinks your friends poured this week that you have not unlocked, built from feed plus useIsUnlocked (store/collection.ts:329), each card the catalog photo (drinkPhoto) or the friend's photo, a Playfair name and the rarity word. Everything comes from the store, so no proof is invented.

First-run Home: replace the template with a 'Start your Dex' spread. One full-bleed catalog photograph as the hero (decoded at view size), a Playfair 34 headline, and a row of 3-5 classics from assets/drinks linking to /drink/[id]. Keep a single Find friends action and drop the duplicate tile.
A footer that closes the feed in Sipply's own words, e.g. 'That's every pour from the last 7 days', with Log a pour. Avoid Instagram's 'You're all caught up', which is its copy.
Tint the refresh: `refreshControl={<RefreshControl tintColor={colors.wine} .../>}`. A one-line change.
Shorten the head so post 1's action row clears the bar on first paint, or accept the overlap and put the drink nameplate on the photo (see PostCard), so the first screen still names what was poured.

screens.name: Feed post (PostCard)
screens.what_it_looks_like_now: No card chrome and no fill: the post sits on cream. The author row is 56pt min with a 16pt gutter and 12pt gap: a 32pt avatar (wine disc with Playfair initials, or the photo), then two stacked text lines. Line 1 is the username in Inter SemiBold 14/18 ink. Line 2 is the drink name in Playfair SemiBold 14/18 ink followed by the dex number '#0042' in Inter Medium 11/14, tracked 1.5, taupeInk (PostCard.tsx:870-883, theme.ts:403-410). A muted 24pt 'more' glyph sits on the right. Then a full-bleed square-cornered 3:4 photo, 440x587, on the bgSunk #E9E5DF placeholder with a 150ms fade (891-895). A gallery adds a 22pt reelScrim '1/3' marker top-right. A post with no photo becomes a square 440x440 panel of category wash (cocktail #F5E6E5 pink, spirit #ECE7E3 grey) with vector glassware at 56% width (744-746). The action row is 44pt: ink outline heart and share on the left and a bookmark on the right, all 24pt; the heart fills wine when liked and pops on change. Under it: '12 likes' in Inter SemiBold 14, the caption in Inter 14/20 clamped to 2 lines with a muted 'more', and '2 hours ago' in Inter 12/16 muted. Then 16pt of padding before the next author row. A double tap shows an 88pt bone heart that pops and fades.
bland_problems: One size does everything. Five of the card's seven type sizes are 14 (username 872, drink name 880, likes 948, caption 955, 'more' 970), time is 12 (978) and the marker 11 (914). Username, drink, like count and caption all read at the same volume, so the card has no hierarchy below the photo.

The drink, which is the collectible and the point of the app, is a 14pt line in the header (687-697), the same size as the username. Playfair at 14 reads as body serif, not display, so the brand face never reaches display size in the feed.

Rarity is invisible. Drink.rarity exists (types.ts:57) and RARITY_META (theme.ts:675-720) defines text-safe tier colours and frames that climb to a gilt 2.5pt edge, but PostCard uses neither, so a legendary pour and a common one are pixel-identical. Gilt, the brand's one metal, never appears on any social surface.
The no-photo fallback is a pink or grey square with clip-art glassware (744-746), even though drinkPhoto(id) in src/data/drinkPhotos.ts has a real studio photograph for 162 drinks.

Nothing on the card makes the viewer want to collect. There is no 'in your Dex / not yet', no subcategory or glassware, no 'first time' moment, though useIsUnlocked (store/collection.ts:329) is one call away.

Weak post boundaries. `card: { paddingBottom: space.lg }` (855) is the only thing between two posts: 16pt of cream, then the next 32pt avatar, so a 12pt muted timestamp runs straight into the next author.
The only colour outside the photo is a filled wine heart and the taupe dex number. Every glyph is ink outline at 24pt (773-793) on cream.
The double-tap reward is an 88pt bone heart (217): Instagram's white-heart gesture in a warmer white, not a Sipply moment.
opportunities: A drink nameplate on the photo's lower edge: a bottom scrim from reelScrimMid to reelScrimClear (tokens already exist for markers on media) carrying the drink name in Playfair 22-24 reelInk, the dex number, and the rarity word. The name becomes the caption of the picture, like a museum label, the photo stays full-bleed, and the header line can drop to just the username. Cap it with maxFontSizeMultiplier like the other overlays on media, and keep the header line as the VoiceOver path.

Rarity as material. In the drink line, add the tier word in RARITY_META[tier].color, which is text-safe on cream. Rare and legendary posts get their RARITY_META edge as a full-bleed rule along the photo's bottom (2pt wineSoft, or 2.5pt gilt plus the giltGlyph sparkle). If any motion is used, reuse FoilSweep (DexCard.tsx:134-160) once and only on a legendary nameplate. Its resting position is off the band, so it can never hide anything.

A 'New to your Dex' tag when useIsUnlocked(drink.id) is false: a 22pt rounded-rectangle tag (radius.badge, 1pt wine edge, wine text) at the right of the action row that opens /drink/[id]. This turns the feed into the collection engine.
Fall back to drinkPhoto(drink.id) before DrinkArt for posts without a photo (expo-image, enforceEarlyResizing, 3:4), and keep DrinkArt only for the 1,927 drinks with no photograph.

Build a real hierarchy: drink 22+ Playfair (on the photo or under it), username 14 SemiBold, likes 14 tabular, caption 15/22, time 12. Separate posts with space.xl to space.xxl, or a full-width hairline.
Make the double-tap burst Sipply's own, e.g. a wine-filled heart with a 2pt bone outline so it holds over any photo. It must stay unmounted at rest on a JS timer, as now.

Optional, scroll-linked: a gentle parallax inside the photo frame. Make the image about 8% taller than the 3:4 frame and translate it ±16pt from one shared list scroll value. Translate 0 is the resting state, so a stall leaves the photo whole. Only do this if a Release-build profile shows no frame drops.

screens.name: Today's pours row
screens.what_it_looks_like_now: A horizontal ScrollView on cream with 12pt vertical padding, a 16pt gutter and 12pt gaps, closed by a hairline rule (296-304). Each tile is a 72x90 rounded rectangle (radius 8, TILE_W/TILE_H at 38-39) holding the person's newest pour, photo inset 3pt and decoded at tile size. Unseen tiles have a 2pt wine frame and seen ones a 1pt #D9CFC1 line (211, 229). Under each tile is the username in Inter 12/16, centred, ink if unseen and muted if seen (328-335). Your tile comes first, with a 22pt square wine + badge hanging off its corner (338-350). With no pour today it is a bgSunk box with a 22pt + glyph labelled 'Log a pour' (270-291), and a 'Find friends' bgSunk box when nobody else has poured. About 5.3 tiles show across 440pt.
bland_problems: The row sits on the same cream as the bar and the feed, separated only by a hairline (296-299), so 'today' has no presence and does not read as a distinct shelf.

The tiles are small for what they carry: 72x90 (38-39) leaves a photo of about 66x84pt, and at that size you cannot tell a Negroni from an Americano. The label names the person but never the drink (257-262), so the row shows who poured without saying what.
The action tiles are grey boxes with a glyph (282-284, frameAction 312-318): the first thing a new user sees in the row is a sunk grey rectangle.
Everything is centred 12pt Inter, and seen tiles drop to muted ink. A row of mostly-seen tiles is a row of grey captions under thumbnails.
opportunities: Make the row the back bar: a wineDeep band (see Home), with bone 2pt frames for unseen and wineSoft 1pt for seen, so the thickness cue survives and the frames read as lit bottles on a shelf.
Larger tiles, 88x110 or 96x120. They are still decoded at view size with enforceEarlyResizing: 50 tiles at about 96pt is a few MB, far under the 256 MB cap.
A second label line with the drink in Playfair 12-13, or the dex number in the dexNumber style, so the row says what was poured.
Your own tile when you have not poured: your last logged drink's catalog photo (drinkPhoto), dimmed, with the + badge, instead of a grey box, so even an empty row has a picture.

screens.name: Today's pours viewer
screens.what_it_looks_like_now: An iOS page-sheet modal on the reel ground #0E0B0B (329) with a light status bar. At the top, one 2pt progress bar per pour with 4pt gaps, bone for shown and 24% bone for ahead (214-225). Then a 48pt header: 32pt avatar, username in Inter SemiBold 14 bone, '2h' in Inter 13 muted bone, and a close MediaIconButton (227-245). The stage (flex 1, about 716pt tall) shows the photo with contentFit contain (318), so a 440x587 3:4 pour sits with about 65pt black bands above and below. Invisible tap zones cover it, left 33% for back and the rest for next. The footer is the drink name in Playfair 22/28 bone with the dex number in muted bone, then 'View post' in Inter SemiBold 14 muted (266-290). Each step is an instant cut. A pour whose photo will not sign shows a 160pt vector glass on black (322).
bland_problems: Black letterbox bands around every contained photo (318, stage 361). The most immersive screen in the area frames each pour in dead black, with no colour from the photo carried into the ground.

The footer is two lines of text on black (266-290): no rarity, no caption, no like count, no Dex status. The drink name at 22pt is the largest type in the social area apart from the wordmark, and it is still modest for a full-screen moment.
The layout is the generic story-viewer template (progress bars, avatar, name, time, close) with nothing of Sipply in it, no wine and no gilt.
The fallback is vector clip-art on black (322) rather than the catalog photograph.
opportunities: A blurred backdrop drawn from the same photo: a second expo-image laid out tiny (about 55x73pt, so enforceEarlyResizing decodes about 165x220px), with blurRadius, scaled up by transform to fill the stage behind the contained photo. The letterbox takes the drink's own colour at almost no memory cost, and it is static, so nothing can hide.

A proper label in the footer: the drink in Playfair 28-34, the rarity word (gilt #B08A3E on #0E0B0B is about 6:1, so it is text-safe on this ground; verify in check-contrast), subcategory and glassware, and the post's caption and likes, joined from the feed store by pour.postId.
A bottom scrim (reelScrimMid to clear) running from the photo into the footer, so photo and label read as one object instead of picture plus caption band.
A 'Not in your Dex yet' action, via useIsUnlocked, beside 'View post'.
Catalog photo before DrinkArt for the fallback.

screens.name: Activity
screens.what_it_looks_like_now: A pushed screen with no tab bar, on cream (379). The bar is cream: a back chevron and 'Activity' in Inter SemiBold 17 centred. Two sections, 'New' and 'Earlier', each headed by SectionHeader size 'group': Inter SemiBold 14 in muted ink, inset 16 (185, ui.tsx:2214-2216). Every row is identical: min 64pt with 12pt padding (384-391), a 40pt avatar, one sentence in Inter 14/20 ('ana liked your pour of Negroni. 2h', name SemiBold, time muted; 402-409), and on the right either a 44pt thumbnail of the liked photo (radius 4, 1pt line; 410-419) or a 36pt filled wine 'Follow' button (or tonal 'Following') (PeopleList.tsx:66-73). Hairline separators are inset to the text. About 12 rows fit on screen.
bland_problems: Every row has one shape (283-322), whether someone liked your Negroni or followed you, and nothing is grouped (the header comment at 27-28 says so). Ten likes on one pour are ten identical rows.

'New' is labelled in the quietest ink: group headers are textMuted (ui.tsx:2216). New rows look exactly like earlier ones, though the app already has an unseen language, the 2pt wine frame on Today's pours.

The loudest objects are 'Follow' CTAs. Each follow row ends in a filled wine button, so a run of followers becomes a column of wine rectangles, while the likes, which are the reward, get a 44pt thumbnail (410-419).
The drink is named in Inter regular inside the sentence (279-280), the one place in the app where a drink name is not set in Playfair.
Cream page, 14pt text, 40pt circles, 44pt squares: nothing here feels like a bar or a collection.
opportunities: Group by post: one row per liked pour, with 2-3 overlapping 24pt avatars (circles are allowed for avatars), the sentence 'ana, leo and 3 others liked your Negroni' with Negroni in Playfair, and the pour's photo at 56-64pt. Group follows into one '4 new followers' row that expands.
A real-data hero at the top: your most-liked pour this month as a wide photo with the count in Playfair ('14 people raised a glass to your Negroni'), all from the fetched items.
Mark new with the same cue as Today's pours: 'New' header in ink, and new rows with a 2pt wine leading edge or a wineWash ground.
Make Follow a 1pt lineInk secondary, and keep filled wine for 'Follow back' only, so the photos carry the colour.
Set the drink name in the sentence in fonts.display with a nested Text.

screens.name: Single post
screens.what_it_looks_like_now: Cream screen (194). The top bar has a back chevron and 'Post' in Inter SemiBold 17 (150-153). The content is a ScrollView holding exactly one PostCard (174-187): the 56pt author row, the 587pt 3:4 photo, actions, likes, caption and time, which fills about one screen on a Pro Max. A post with no photo shows the 440pt square art panel, which leaves about 250pt of empty cream below. Loading, error and missing states are the shared EmptyState and Hold.
bland_problems: This is where the profile grid, Saved, Activity and the viewer all land, and it shows the same card as the feed and nothing else (174-187). A dedicated post screen adds no context about the drink, its rarity or its place in your Dex.
The generic 'Post' title (151) and cream bar make it indistinguishable from Settings-class screens.
A no-photo post leaves a large empty cream area under a pink square.
opportunities: A 'From the Dex' plate under the card: catalog photo (drinkPhoto) or DrinkArt on the CATEGORY_META fieldFrom/fieldTo gradient, the name in Playfair 28, dex number, RarityBadge (ui.tsx:523), 2-3 tasting notes, 'In your Dex' or 'Not in your Dex yet', and a bordered 'Open in the Dex' button.
'More pours of this drink' from the feed already in the store (filter by drinkId, no new query): a 3-up square grid with layout.gridGap, each tile decoded at tile size.
Optionally title the bar with the drink name. Note this bends the 'Playfair only for the wordmark in bars' rule in ScreenTopBar.tsx:25-27, so it is Jan's call.

screens.name: Chrome: floating tab bar and top bar
screens.what_it_looks_like_now: Tab bar: a white #FFFFFF rectangle inset 12pt from each side and floating 36pt above the bottom edge. It has radius 12, a 1pt #D9CFC1 edge and a tight 4/14 shadow, and is about 64pt tall (333-343). Four equal slots: Home, Dex, a 48x36 filled wine + rectangle (404-413), and Profile with your 24pt face. Glyphs are 24pt in muted ink at rest; the active tab is espresso, solid, with an 11pt SemiBold label (228, 298, 394-397). The same paper bar sits on every tab. The dark skin (reelBar #2B2322, 75-82, 345-348) is used only on Reels. Top bar: on every screen, a 44pt cream row with 26pt ink glyph buttons and a centred Inter SemiBold 17 title, and a 1pt rule that switches on after 1pt of scroll (97-131, 256-262). Home alone swaps the title for the wordmark.
bland_problems: The bar is the same white slab on every paper screen (339-343). Over Home's full-bleed photos it reads as a white box laid over the picture, and on cream it is a white rectangle on a cream rectangle.
The chrome's only wine is the 48x36 + (404-413), and its only state cue is a glyph swap plus a label weight.

One top bar for every screen (ScreenTopBar.tsx:19-23) is good discipline, but there is no tone or subtitle variation, so Activity and Post have the same furniture as Settings, and there is no way to give Home's head a different ground.
opportunities: Use the existing espresso skin on every tab, not just Reels. The DARK colours are already contrast-checked: reelInk active, reelInkDim at rest about 5.9:1, bone + with a wine plus. That puts one dark, anchored object on every cream screen and stops the white-box-over-photo effect. It is a one-condition change at FloatingTabBar.tsx:198-200; check it on device against the shadow rule.
A 2pt indicator (stroke.indicator) above the active slot, as an extra cue that does not rely on colour.
Add `tone` ('paper' | 'wine') and an optional `subtitle` to ScreenTopBar, so Home's head can sit on wineDeep and Activity can say 'Last 30 days' without hand-built bars.

cross_cutting: One ground everywhere: cream #F7F2EA plus 3.5% grain. 19 route files set `backgroundColor: colors.bg`, the top bar repeats it (ScreenTopBar.tsx:257), and the only other ground in the social area is the black viewer. Wine and wineDeep never appear as a surface, only as 2pt frames, a dot, a filled heart, the wordmark and the 48x36 +.

14pt Inter does nearly all the talking. Username, drink name, like count, caption, 'more', the Activity sentence and the viewer username are all 14 (PostCard.tsx:872/880/948/955/970, activity.tsx:404, pours:349). Playfair, the display face, is set at 14 in the feed (PostCard.tsx:880) and reaches display size only in the wordmark (28) and the viewer (22).

The collectible layer is missing from the social layer. Rarity (types.ts:57, RARITY_META theme.ts:675-720), gilt, FoilSweep (DexCard.tsx:134), RarityBadge (ui.tsx:523) and the viewer's own Dex status (useIsUnlocked, store/collection.ts:329) appear on no feed, row, Activity or post surface. The dex number in 11pt taupe is the only hint that a pour belongs to a Dex.

Real photography is unused. No file in this area imports drinkPhoto (src/data/drinkPhotos.ts, 162 studio photographs). Every fallback is vector DrinkArt on a category wash: PostCard 56% width (744-746), tiles 44pt (TodaysPours.tsx:252-253), Activity 30pt, viewer 160pt (pours:322).

Cadence never changes. Feed cells, Activity rows and pours tiles are each one repeated shape. There are no interleaved modules, no grouping, no summaries and no closing footers, so length equals sameness.

One empty-state template everywhere (ui.tsx:1984): a 36pt glyph, 22pt title, 16pt body and a button, used by Home, Activity, Post and the viewer. The first-run Home, the most-seen empty state, is the blandest screen in the app.
One edge everywhere: the 1pt #D9CFC1 line draws the tile frames, thumbnails, tab bar, row hairlines and the rule under the bar. Gilt, the frame reserved to mean something, is never drawn here.

Ink outline glyphs on cream for every control (24pt in the card, 26pt in the bar), with wine kept for tiny accents. The result is correct and quiet, but nothing on the page has visual weight apart from the photographs.

The safe kinds of motion the constraints allow (scroll-linked transforms, parallax that cannot hide content, press feedback) are unused on Home. The only motion is the like pop and the double-tap burst.
Pull to refresh on Home is the untinted system spinner (index.tsx:256-257), while Reels tints its own (reels.tsx:157).

critiques.area: The collection: Dex tab grid, Dex card, drink detail page, Stats, My Bar, and the DrinkArt/DrinkPanels pieces they share. Read-only critique of branch perf-fixes (build 13), reconstructed for an iPhone 17 Pro Max (440 x 956 pt). I also measured the 162 drink photos and the drink data with scripts.

screens.name: Dex tab (collection grid)
screens.what_it_looks_like_now: Cream #F7F2EA ground with the 3.5% grain (dex.tsx:933, Grain.tsx:62). A fixed 44pt bar: 'Dex' centred in Inter SemiBold 20 and a 26pt stats glyph on the right (dex.tsx:812-823). Under it is a 2pt progress rule: #E9E5DF track, wine fill set to collected/2,089 (dex.tsx:829-834, 945-952). At 20 entries the fill is about 4pt wide; at 0 it is nothing. The list header stacks four chrome rows. (1) A white 44pt search field with a 1pt #D9CFC1 edge (dex.tsx:692). (2) The line '0 of 2,089 collected' in 13pt textMuted (dex.tsx:703-705, 975-983). (3) A 64pt white Settings-style ListGroup row: bottle icon, 'My Bar' in 16 regular, a 13pt subtitle, a chevron (dex.tsx:721-738). (4) A text-tab filter row: 'All 2,089 / Cocktails 899 / Spirits 1,190 | All / Collected / Not yet' in 13pt SemiBold with 11pt counts and a 2pt underline (dex.tsx:750-797). A hairline closes the header (dex.tsx:799). The header is about 255pt, so the first card starts near y=363 and the first screen shows about 1.7 rows. The grid is two columns of 200 x 278pt cards with an 8pt gap and 8pt corners (dex.tsx:71-74, 517-520; DexCard.tsx:439-443). The order is fixed by Dex number: #0001-#0150 are all cocktails and all photographed. Then #0151-#0529 are 379 spirits in a row, almost none photographed, drawn as vector recesses: a #E3DDD3 to #D8D1C5 gradient, a 132pt espresso-ink glass silhouette, the 11pt number and a 12pt Inter muted name over a slot-coloured fade (DexCard.tsx:284-294, 359-363, 389-424). For a new user every card is locked: an 11pt lock glyph top right (DexCard.tsx:354) and a 1pt taupe edge (DexCard.tsx:447-451). There is no focal point, no featured entry, no section break, and nothing changes from row 1 to row 1,044.
bland_problems: The collection has no hero. Progress is a 2pt rule (dex.tsx:829-834) and one 13pt muted sentence (dex.tsx:703-705, 975-983). The one number the screen exists for is the smallest type on it, while the Settings-style My Bar row (dex.tsx:721-738) gets 64pt.

The header is about 38% of the first screen and is all utility: search, a sentence, a Settings row, text tabs (dex.tsx:684-801). It holds no imagery, nothing you own and no brand. The first thing a collector sees is a form.

The order does not change, so the material does not change for hundreds of rows. Dex numbers 1-150 are all photos and 151-529 are 379 consecutive spirits in vector (DRINKS is sorted by dexNumber in src/data/index.ts:7-9). Measured: 60% of the 1,190 spirits resolve to two glass shapes (427 rocks, 288 glencairn; glasses.ts:186-210). On the Spirits filter only 12 of 1,190 entries have a photo, so that tab is a wall of near-identical tumbler silhouettes.

Every locked vector card is drawn in the same ink. The liquid is always lockInkSoft #4A3B38, the vessel is lockInk at 0.18, and garnish is suppressed (artwork/index.tsx:142-144, 165-166). A Negroni, a Mezcal and a Scotch read as the same dark brown block in different glasses. The 23-colour LIQUID palette (liquid.ts:17-41), the one thing that tells drinks apart, never reaches the grid for 99%+ of a new user's cards.

The grid's ground and the locked card's ground are the same family. The slot #E3DDD3 is 1.08:1 against the cream page (theme.ts:183-185), and the 1pt taupe edge is decorative at 1.68:1 (theme.ts:141). The board reads as faint beige rectangles on beige rather than a display case.

No sections across 2,089 entries. Subcategory is in the data (47 values: Scotch 125, Rum 112, Gin 95, Brandy 86, Agave 63...) but the grid is one undivided FlatList (dex.tsx:836-893). There are no chapters, no 'you are in the Scotch aisle', no landmarks to orient by while scrolling.

Filters are text tabs at caption size (dex.tsx:1067-1087). Fine as utility, but they are the only thing on screen that says 'Cocktails' or 'Spirits', in 13pt muted, with no category colour except a 2pt underline.
opportunities: Turn the header into a cabinet front. Lead with a large Playfair figure ('14', type.display 36 or larger; the 36 size is used today only in PasswordResetOverlay.tsx:297) over 'of 2,089' in Inter. Put a static strip of the user's last 3-5 caught card faces beside or under it (their own pour photos, decoded with enforceEarlyResizing at about 64pt). This is plain static layout with no entrance animation. As a scroll-linked effect, the figure and strip can collapse into the 44pt bar (translate/scale from scrollY). That is safe because the resting state is fully visible.

Give the long scroll chapters. Switch to a SectionList by category, then subcategory, with sticky Playfair 20-22 headers that carry a count, e.g. 'Scotch  3 of 125'. Each header could hold a thin full-width category band (merlot for mixed, espresso for distilled, per theme.ts:589-596). Sticky headers are native and not an entrance animation. This breaks the 379-spirit run into readable shelves.

Break the two-column rhythm on purpose. Every 6-8 rows, insert one full-width 'feature' cell: a photographed drink, the user's rarest, a legendary with its foil, or 'You can make this tonight' from matchOwned. Mount only one at a time in the window (windowSize is 5, dex.tsx:885-888), so the 256MB image budget is untouched.

Colour the ghosts. Draw locked vector cards with each drink's own liquidColor at heavy desaturation, or in that hue's ink, instead of one lockInkSoft for all. Turn on the embossLight/embossShadow pair (theme.ts:187-189), which is defined and used by no screen, as a debossed outline, so an empty slot reads as a stamped impression of that specific drink.

Move My Bar out of the header list into a destination with weight. One option is a wide card with the shelf's count as a figure ('48 you can pour') over a row of glass silhouettes. Another is a pinned row under the cabinet front. Either way, not a Settings ListRow in the collection's most valuable spot.

Consider one darker ground for this tab only (a 'back-bar' cabinet in wineDeep #3E0A12 or espresso), with cards as lit objects. Tokens would need adding next to the reel set, which theme.ts:191-197 reserves for video, and every pair re-audited by check-contrast. The grey studio photos would read as lit plinths on dark. Offer it as one direction, not a default, since 'dark luxury' is its own cliche.

The Playfair drink name, the brand's voice, is set at caption size and reads like a filename under a thumbnail. The number is 11pt (theme.ts:403-410). The card has no typographic anchor at all.

Grey studio photos sit on a warm cream app. The neutral backdrop (#C5C6C5) is darker and cooler than the page (#F7F2EA), and the white fog over the bottom 76pt turns the foot of each photo milky grey (DexCard.tsx:393-398). These read as stock product shots on a light background, not a speakeasy or a collectible.

Rarity is not legible at a glance. Common's frame is #EFE9E0, 1.08:1 on the page and 1.21:1 on white (theme.ts:94-95, 693-694), so it is invisible. Uncommon's taupe and rare's wineSoft at 1.5-2pt only show next to each other. The tier shows mainly as an 8pt dot (DexCard.tsx:344-351). With 646 rares and 229 legendaries in the index, a collector cannot scan for them.

The card has no card anatomy. There is no title plate, no number stamp, no tier band and no back, just a picture with a caption fade. Nothing says trading card, cigar band, bottle label or menu card, which are the speakeasy collectible references the brand name points to.

Collected vector cards are almost white. fieldFrom is #FFFAF8 or #FBF9F7 (theme.ts:626, 636), so a collected drawing looks like a blank white card with a small illustration on it, paler and weaker than the locked recess beside it.
opportunities: Give the card a nameplate and stamp. Set the drink name in Playfair 16-18 on collected cards (cap Dynamic Type as now, DexCard.tsx:404-411). Set the Dex number as a small embossed plate or tab (radius.badge, 1pt edge) rather than loose 11pt text. Put the rarity word in that plate on rare and legendary, so the tier is said in words on the card itself and not only in a pip.

Make collecting a material change, not a 3% one. Locked: drained photo plus a debossed or blind-stamped look (emboss tokens, theme.ts:187-189), name in Inter muted, no plate. Collected: the full nameplate, the tier frame drawn as a double rule (outer tier colour, 2pt bone gap, inner hairline), and the user's own pour photo as the face, which already happens at DexCard.tsx:209-214. Re-grade the photo pipeline instead of the card. scripts/build-drink-photos.mjs already bakes the locked variant, so it could also bake a warm grade of each collected photo: lift the backdrop toward bone or deepen it toward espresso. Then photos and cream page share a colour temperature. The 'more coming' batch is the moment to brief a warmer or darker backdrop.

Raise the collected vector field. Use the actual category wash or a merlot/espresso ground with the glass lit in colour, instead of a near-white gradient, so a collected drawing looks richer than an empty slot, not paler.

Press feedback that feels like handling an object: PressableScale 0.97 already exists (theme.ts:583). Optionally add a very small scroll-linked shift of the photo inside its frame (a few points of translateY from the list's scrollY). It is a transform from the resting state, so it cannot hide content. It must be one cheap shared value, not a per-cell listener, given 2,089 cells.
Keep FoilSweep for legendaries but give it a target: a gilt nameplate edge. Right now the sweep runs over a grey photo under a 2.5pt border.

The milestone ladder leaves most users at one rung for months. Rung 2 is 10% of 2,089, about 209 drinks (milestones.ts: 'Barfly in Training'). Draw the whole Dex as one completion board: 2,089 small square cells (radius 0-2, not ovals) in Dex order, lit by category or tier where collected, empty slot tone where not. Draw it as ONE Svg path per state (or one Skia canvas), not 2,089 views. Below it, on a 16pt gutter, sits an 86pt circular avatar: a photo, or a wine disc with Playfair initials. To its right is the display name in Inter SemiBold 14, and under that three equal columns of counts: the figure in Inter SemiBold 16 tabular, the word in Inter 14 ink. The bio is Inter 14 ink. Next comes an action row: two equal 36pt tonal rectangles (bone #E9E5DF fill, #D9CFC1 1pt edge, 14pt semibold labels 'Edit profile' and 'Share profile') and a 36pt bone square with the add-person glyph. opportunities: Give the name the focal role without breaking Instagram's structure. Set the display name at 22pt Inter SemiBold (textRole.emptyTitle) on its own line under the avatar and counts row, as IG puts the name under the avatar. Counts and bio stay at 14-16. Switch the accent on. Draw the 86pt avatar with `ring` in person.accent, and make initials use accent as their fill, as the type already promises. Each profile then gets one personal colour that is not the brand's.

Fill IG's highlights slot the Sipply way with a 'shelf' row. A horizontal strip of small rounded-rectangle Dex cards (about 64x84, radius.control) for this person's rarest shared drinks: derivePostStats and drinksByDexNumber in DexShelf.tsx already compute these. Give the own-profile empty state imagery. Show a 3-up 'ghost' row of baked drained stock photos (drinkPhotoLocked, assets/drinks/locked/) under 'Your first pours land here'. It is static, needs no entrance animation, and has three small decodes.

Duplicated capture UI. log.tsx:649-684 and add-drink.tsx:1366-1412 draw the same 4:3 bone sunk well with a camera glyph and the same two equal outlined buttons. The pour photo is always an inset attachment, never the hero, in the two screens where it is created.

critiques.area:
Everything around the content in Sipply (repo root /Users/janmcqueeny/Projects/drinkdex-worktrees/polish, branch perf-fixes, build 13): sign-in and its sub-steps, the username step, the Welcome step, the password-reset overlay, the intro film and the reduced-motion intro, loading holds, Settings, Edit profile, the shared EmptyState, the design system (theme.ts, ui.tsx, ScreenTopBar.tsx, icons.tsx, Grain.tsx), and an inventory of every visual asset. This was a read-only review. I rebuilt each screen from the code for an iPhone 17 Pro Max (440x956pt, about 62pt safe area at the top and 34pt at the bottom). Paths in the findings are relative to the repo root.

The short version: the most immersive things the app owns are the wax seal and the merlot pour in the intro film, and these screens never use them again. A first-time user watches a rich merlot film, then it dissolves over 280ms into a flat cream form. That form tops out at 17pt Inter, and its most saturated pixels are Google's and Facebook's logo colours. Every screen in this area is built from one recipe: a cream page, a white box with a 1pt line and a 12pt corner, Inter at 13 to 17pt, a bare 1.75-stroke glyph, and a single wine button. Not one drink photo, seal, glass drawing or wine-coloured surface appears in any of them.

screens.name: Sign-in, first step ("Sign in or join Sipply")
screens.what_it_looks_like_now:
Home is the first tab and it is gated, so this is the first screen a new user sees after the film. It is cream #F7F2EA from edge to edge, with Grain on top at roughly 4/255 luminance, which is invisible.

Top to bottom:
- y 0-62: a cream status-bar band.
- y 62-106: a 44pt cream bar. On the left is a 26pt espresso close X. In the centre is "Sign in or join Sipply" in Inter SemiBold 17, with a 1pt #D9CFC1 rule that is always drawn.
- 32pt gap.
- A white grouped box with a 1pt #8A7F74 edge and an 8pt corner. Its first row is "Country or region", 56pt: a 12pt Inter Medium muted label over a 16pt value "United States (+1)" and a chevron. Then a 1pt rule, then "Phone number", 56pt, with its label resting at 16pt.
- A two-line 13pt muted hint.
- 24pt gap, then a full-width 48pt wine Continue button. It is disabled at 42% opacity until the number is valid, so on first view it reads as a dusty rose (about #B69393).
- 24pt gap, then the "or" divider: 1pt rules around a 13pt muted word.
- 24pt gap, then four identical 48pt white buttons with a 1pt espresso edge, 12pt apart: email, Apple, Google, Facebook. Each has a 20pt mark pinned at the left and a centred 16pt SemiBold label.
- A three-line 13pt muted consent paragraph, centred.
- About 100pt of empty cream.
- The floating white tab bar, 64pt, with its wine log tile.

The brand appears only as the word "Sipply" inside a 17pt Inter title. There is no image. The type spans 12 to 17pt. Below the bar, everything is a stack of rectangles of the same width.
bland_problems: The handoff from the film is the biggest drop in the app. The clip ends on a full merlot field with the gilt wax seal, then dissolves in 280ms (src/components/VideoIntro.tsx:68-71, 87, 142-147) into this cream form. Nothing on the form carries the merlot or the seal forward, so the film reads as a splash ad rather than as a door into the place.

There is no brand at all. The wordmark, the seal and the tagline are absent. The only mention of the name is the bar title "Sign in or join Sipply" (src/components/auth/SignInScreen.tsx:69), set in Inter SemiBold 17 like every other bar (src/constants/theme.ts:347, src/components/ScreenTopBar.tsx:124). The password-reset overlay is the only auth surface that shows the wordmark (src/components/PasswordResetOverlay.tsx:200).

The brand is outshouted. With Continue dimmed to 42% (src/components/auth/SignInScreen.tsx:155, src/components/ui.tsx:2117), the most saturated pixels on screen are Google's four mark colours and Facebook's #0866FF (src/components/auth/ProviderButton.tsx:129-133). On the first screen, the strongest colour belongs to other companies.

There is no focal point. Below the bar, about 70% of the screen is five 48pt full-width rectangles and two 56pt field rows of the same width, all a 1pt line on white (src/components/auth/ProviderButton.tsx:163-173, src/components/ui.tsx:2101-2110). Nothing is larger or richer than anything else.

The type span is 12 to 17pt. The largest text on the page is the bar title. The fields, buttons and consent are 12, 13 and 16pt Inter (src/constants/theme.ts:345-359, src/components/auth/Consent.tsx:103-113).
The bottom half ends in about 100pt of blank cream above the floating tab bar (src/components/auth/SignInScreen.tsx:240, 251). The screen is not filled. It just stops.

The bar's rule is always on (src/components/auth/AuthTitleBar.tsx:51-58) and sits on a cream bar over a cream page (src/components/ScreenTopBar.tsx:256-262). The page reads as a settings form, not a front door.
opportunities: Make the sign-in a sheet laid over the film's last frame. Keep Jan's layout exactly: title bar, grouped country and phone box, Continue, "or", outlined providers. Put it on a cream panel with radius.card top corners and a 1pt line edge, starting about 38% down the screen. Above it, show a static still of the film's final frame: merlot with the seal. That could be a new assets/images/intro-end.webp extracted from assets/video/intro.mp4 at 4.9s and decoded with enforceEarlyResizing, or a wineDeep ground with scripts/icon/mark-seal-coupe.png. The film's existing 280ms dissolve then becomes a match-cut onto the same merlot and seal, and nothing new has to animate in.

Put the Playfair wordmark (allowed: it is the wordmark) in bone on the merlot hero at type.display 36 or larger. Bone on wineDeep is 13.32:1 and already audited in scripts/check-contrast.mjs as "intro wordmark (bone) on wine-deep". Under it, one sentence-case Inter line of real copy, the App Store subtitle "Collect every drink you try.", in taupe (8.90:1 on wineDeep). No caps, no tracking.

Make the hero the ScrollView's first child, not a fixed header. It then scrolls away under the keyboard, at large Dynamic Type sizes and on small phones, and can never cover the form. A scroll-linked translateY parallax on the still, as a transform from its resting position, is allowed and cannot hide content. Hide the image from VoiceOver. The step title stays the bar's header, so the flow is announced as it is today.

Write the "one wine thing per view" rule down as "one wine CONTROL". A wine ground is a place, not an action, so Continue on the cream sheet stays the only wine control. Consider giving Continue full strength with an explanatory hint instead of the 42% fade, so the brand colour is not a washed rose on first sight.

Keep the provider stack exactly as it is. It is Jan's layout, and Apple, Google and Meta require those marks. Once the merlot hero exists, the third-party colours stop being the loudest thing on screen.

screens.name: Sign-in sub-steps (phone code, email, password, reset, sign in another way) and the country picker
screens.what_it_looks_like_now:
Each step swaps in instantly on the same cream page under the same 17pt bar, which shows back or close and the step's own title ("Confirm your number", "Welcome back", "Create your account"). A 14pt muted lede comes first, then either six white 56pt code cells with 1pt #8A7F74 edges and 22pt Inter SemiBold digits, or a white field group. Then a 48pt wine button, then 13pt wine text links ("Send a new code in 0:42", "Forgot your password?"), with Notice boxes in wineWash or dangerWash.

The country picker is a native page sheet: a cream list of about 240 rows in 16pt Inter with hairline separators, under a 14pt muted group header, with Grain added locally. Every step has the same anatomy and colour; only the words change.
bland_problems: Steps are told apart only by a 17pt title. "Welcome back" and "Create your account" are opposite moments, one a return and one a first arrival, and they are drawn identically (src/components/auth/SignInScreen.tsx:76-86, 219-245).

The verification code, the one moment of suspense in sign-in, is six white boxes in the app's generic input skin (src/components/auth/PhoneCodeStep.tsx:239-266), with nothing else on the page but text.
Every lede is set in the same 14pt muted Inter (src/components/auth/PhoneCodeStep.tsx:228-234, src/components/auth/EmailSteps.tsx:316-322), so the instructions have no voice.
opportunities: Carry a compact version of the entry step's merlot hero through every step: a 96 to 120pt band with the seal at about 48pt above the sheet, so the flow never falls back to bare cream after step one. It is the same static still, scaled down. Nothing new to animate.
"Welcome back" could greet by name once the lookup knows the account. If the lookup returns no display name, keep the plain title rather than inventing one.
Leave the country picker plain on purpose. It is a utility list, and immersion should go into moments, not into every list row.

screens.name: Choose a username (every new account)
screens.what_it_looks_like_now: A cream page with the 17pt bar "Choose a username", no controls and the rule drawn. A 32pt gap, then a 16pt muted lede ("It is how friends find you and how your pours are signed..."). Two stacked white 56pt fields with 16pt gaps: Display name with its hint, then Username with its rule hint. A wine 48pt Continue, a three-line 13pt consent paragraph, and a 14pt wine text button "Not your account? Sign out". The tab bar floats below.
bland_problems: The lede promises that the handle is "how your pours are signed" (src/components/AuthGate.tsx:336-339), but nothing shows a signature. It is two text boxes on cream (src/components/AuthGate.tsx:342-379), so the moment you take up your identity looks like a tax form.

It is the same ground, bar, field skin and wine block as the sign-in step before it and the Welcome step after it (src/components/AuthGate.tsx:416-432). Three steps in a row are visually indistinguishable.
opportunities: Add a live signature preview above the fields: the real PostCard header (avatar 32 with the user's accent ring, display name, @handle) updating as the user types. Better still, a bordered card showing a sample pour signed by them, using a real Dex photo decoded at view size and the drink's name in Playfair, which is allowed. It makes "how your pours are signed" literal and gives the step a focal image.

Alternatively, a member card: a wineDeep panel with radius.card and a 1pt edge, with the seal as a low-opacity decorative mark, the @handle in bone Inter 22, and "Joined" plus the real month from the account's created_at. Use only real data; never invent a member number.

screens.name: Welcome: Find your people
screens.what_it_looks_like_now: A cream page with the 17pt bar "Find your people". A bare 28pt espresso `users` glyph, then a two-line 16pt muted lede. Then up to six white Cards with 1pt line edges and a 12pt corner, 16pt apart: Facebook, Friends you already know, Let friends find you, Invite a friend, Find by username, Bring your Instagram friends. Each card is a 20pt glyph and a 16pt SemiBold heading, a 13pt muted body, and an outlined secondary button (contacts is the only filled one). The stack runs about two screens tall. A pinned footer with a 1pt top rule holds a wine Continue above the tab bar.
bland_problems: Six identical cards repeat one anatomy: glyph, 16pt heading, 13pt body, outlined button (src/components/FindFriends.tsx:346-520, styles 544-556). Nothing tells the user which path matters. Only the colour of one button separates the recommended path from the rest.

The header is a bare 28pt `users` glyph (src/components/WelcomeConnect.tsx:71). It is the same glyph used by Home's empty feed (src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx:249) and by the Find friends row in Settings (src/app/settings.tsx:309), so the welcome moment has the same face as an empty list.
It is the first screen after the account exists, and it shows no drinks, no seal and no wine surface. It reads as a permissions checklist.
opportunities: Lead with one hero block for the recommended path (contacts), set larger on a wineDeep or wineWash panel. Fold the other four into a compact ListGroup of rows. That gives the screen a focal point and halves its height.

Replace the bare glyph with brand art that needs no fake people: two DrinkArt glasses (vector, at no memory cost) side by side as a toast, or the seal. Never show placeholder avatars of people who do not exist (Jan's "never invent proof").

screens.name: Password reset overlay (choose a new password, password changed)
screens.what_it_looks_like_now: An opaque cream layer at zIndex 20 over the whole app. It has a 36pt Playfair Bold wine "Sipply" wordmark, the only use of type.display in the app. Below it: a 22pt Inter title, a 16pt muted blurb, two white secondary fields, a wine Set password button and a muted text Cancel. The confirmation is a bare 40pt wine check glyph, a 22pt title, a blurb and Continue, centred on cream.
bland_problems: The "done" mark is a stroked check glyph (src/components/PasswordResetOverlay.tsx:131). It is the same check used on chips and country rows, so a completed account recovery has no more ceremony than ticking a filter.

The overlay renders after <Grain/> in the root fragment (src/app/_layout.tsx, Grain before PasswordResetOverlay) on an opaque ground (src/components/PasswordResetOverlay.tsx:283-291), so it is the one paper surface with no grain at all.
opportunities: Use the seal itself as the confirmation, a static image (scripts/icon/mark-seal-coupe.png bundled at about 96pt): sealed, done. A seal is a round object in a picture, not a UI oval, but never put a glyph inside a wine disc.
Reuse the sign-in merlot hero here as well, so every auth surface shares one front door.

screens.name: Intro film, reduced-motion intro, and the splash handoff
screens.what_it_looks_like_now:
On cold start the native splash shows the seal at 220pt on bone #E9E5DF (app.json:122-126). It dissolves onto the film: a 1080x1920, 5.04s, 24fps H.264 clip of a 3D wax seal with a gilt coupe on tan paper (#D6C4B1). Merlot wax floods up from below until the frame is solid merlot with the seal centred. Tap anywhere skips. It then fades in 280ms to whatever is underneath: the cream sign-in for a new user, the cream Home for a returning one.

With Reduce Motion on, SipplyIntro draws instead. A bone ground, two discs flooding merlot then wine, the Playfair Bold "Sipply" letters scaling in, a 90x2 taupe rule, the tagline "DISCOVER · SIP · SHARE" in 12pt Inter Medium tracked 6pt, and a vignette. A cream disc then opens from the centre.
bland_problems: Three grounds in the first second: splash bone #E9E5DF, film paper #D6C4B1, page cream #F7F2EA (app.json:124, src/constants/theme.ts:265, 78). The code's own note admits the seal also jumps size between splash and film (src/components/VideoIntro.tsx:50-51).

The film is the only place the app is immersive, and it is thrown away. Nothing after it reuses its frames, its merlot or its seal (grep: wineDeep is never a fill, src/components/FloatingTabBar.tsx:409 only, and merlot is a fill only in src/components/SipplyIntro.tsx:319, 345).

It breaks one of Jan's rules: the reduced-motion tagline is literal uppercase with 6pt tracking (src/components/SipplyIntro.tsx:83, src/constants/theme.ts:372-374). check-design only catches textTransform, so a hard-coded caps string gets past it. It also disagrees with the lockup's "DISCOVER. SIP. ENJOY."
opportunities: Match-cut the film's end onto the sign-in hero (see sign-in). The 280ms dissolve stays exactly as it is and gains a destination that continues the scene.

Extract one still from intro.mp4 (the merlot field with the seal, about 4.9s) as a bundled webp. It is the richest single image the app owns, and one still decoded at view size costs about 3 to 8MB of the 256MB cache.

Change the SipplyIntro tagline to sentence case with no tracking, such as "Discover, sip, share", or drop it, and remove label.tagline's 6pt letterSpacing so the brand film obeys the same rule as the app.

screens.name: Loading holds (Hold) on cold start and gated screens
screens.what_it_looks_like_now: Plain cream for 400ms, then a centred system ActivityIndicator in wine. After 8s a 13pt muted line appears ("Still connecting. The Dex and Stats work without a connection."). This is what shows between the film and the app while auth-js starts up (src/components/AuthGate.tsx:208-210), and while a new account's profile row loads.

opportunities: Add a static brand mark above the spinner: the mono seal (scripts/icon/mark-seal-coupe-mono.png) at about 64pt in taupe or wine. A still image cannot stall in a Release build. The phases stay on JS timers as they are now, and the mark is hidden from VoiceOver, so the spoken slow message is unchanged.

screens.name: Settings
screens.what_it_looks_like_now:
A cream page with a 17pt "Settings" bar, a back chevron, and a rule that appears on scroll.

Contents:
- An identity ListGroup: one 64pt white row with a 40pt avatar with its accent ring, the display name in 16pt SemiBold, @handle in 13pt muted, and a chevron.
- Five sections, each with a 14pt SemiBold muted header inset 16pt, and a white ListGroup with a 1pt line edge and 12pt corner. Your activity: Saved, Activity. How people find you: Find friends. Who can reach you: Blocked accounts. About: Help, Privacy, Terms. Account: Reset collection, Sign out, Delete account, all in danger red.
- Each of the 11 rows: a 22pt espresso outline glyph, a 16pt Inter title, a 13pt muted subtitle, an 18pt faint chevron, and hairline separators.
- A centred 13pt muted "Sipply 1.x (13)" at the foot.

The largest type on the screen is the 17pt bar.
bland_problems: Every row has the same anatomy and weight (src/components/ui.tsx:934-1031, styles 2232-2267). The account holder's own row (src/app/settings.tsx:250-273) is the same 64pt row as "Blocked accounts" (src/app/settings.tsx:327-333). The one personal thing on the screen has no presence.
The screen never mentions the collection the account exists for: no Dex count, no rank, no recent pour. It could belong to any app.

The glyph choices are arbitrary: `flame` for Reset collection (src/app/settings.tsx:373), the `profile` silhouette for Sign out (src/app/settings.tsx:381), `close` for Delete account (src/app/settings.tsx:390), `eye` for Privacy (src/app/settings.tsx:346).
The colophon is a bare 13pt caption (src/app/settings.tsx:408-411). It is where an app usually signs off, and it has no mark.
opportunities: Turn the identity row into a member card at the top: a wineDeep panel with radius.card and a 1pt edge. A 64pt avatar with its accent ring, the display name in bone Inter 22, @handle in taupe (8.90:1), and real figures the app already computes: "48 of 2,089 collected" in tabular figures and the rank title. Optionally the seal as a decorative watermark. Tap still opens Edit profile, and the whole card is one VoiceOver button with the same label and hint as today. Gilt stays for legendary only.
Sign off with a colophon: the seal at about 40pt, the version under it, and nothing invented.
Keep the five sections as plain ListGroups. A settings list should stay quiet. The immersion goes into the identity card and the colophon, which also gives the long list a top and a bottom.

screens.name: Edit profile (modal page sheet)
screens.what_it_looks_like_now: A cream page sheet with Grain. A 17pt "Edit profile" bar with a muted Cancel on the left, rule on. A centred 96pt avatar with a 2pt accent ring. Under it, two outlined 48pt buttons, "Choose photo" and "Take photo", and a red text "Remove photo". A 12pt muted "Accent" label, then six 44pt square swatches with 8pt corners, the selected one ringed 2pt in ink. Then three stacked white 56pt fields, Display name, Username with an @ prefix, and a 112pt About, followed by a 13pt "0/300" counter. A full-width wine "Save changes" sits at the foot of the scroll.
bland_problems: The accent choice barely shows. It only tints the avatar's 2pt ring (src/components/ui.tsx:740, src/app/edit-profile.tsx:431-439), so picking Amber or Plum changes about 2pt of colour around a 96pt circle.
The preview is a lone avatar, not the profile people will see. Name, handle and bio are edited blind in generic fields (src/app/edit-profile.tsx:507-546).

It uses the same cream, white-field and wine-block recipe as sign-in and the username step (src/app/edit-profile.tsx:568-631). The page that dresses your public face has no more character than a login.

Engineering aside, not visual: a private ACCENT_NAMES keyed by list position (src/app/edit-profile.tsx:75-82) duplicates theme.ts's exported map (src/constants/theme.ts:777-802), whose own comment says a positional copy breaks silently on a reorder.
opportunities: Replace the bare avatar with a live preview of the real ProfileHeader (avatar, name, @handle, bio, counts) in a bordered card. Edits then show in place: "this is your page".
Give the accent a visible job in the preview, such as a thicker 3pt ring at 96pt, plus the accent as the preview card's top rule. The choice should be seen, not hunted for. Swatches stay squares.

screens.name: Empty states (shared EmptyState, 47 call sites in 19 files)
screens.what_it_looks_like_now:
Every empty or failed list, on paper or on the reels ground, draws the same block: 48pt of top padding, a bare 36pt espresso outline glyph, a 22pt Inter SemiBold title, a 16pt muted body at most 300pt wide, a 200pt-minimum wine button, and an optional small text button.

Glyph counts across the 47 sites: alert 13, search 8, users 6, reels 3, filter 3, dex 3, camera 3, bookmark 2, and heart, eyeOff, check and bottle once each. Home's "Nothing poured yet" uses `users` with "Find friends". Profile's "Log your first pour" uses `camera`. The Dex's "Nothing collected yet" uses `dex`.
bland_problems: One anatomy for every situation (src/components/ui.tsx:1984-2030, styles 2463-2480). An empty Dex, an empty feed, a failed load and a blocked-accounts list are indistinguishable except for a 36pt line glyph and the words.

The most-seen empty states for a new user show no drink. Home's empty feed (src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx:248-253) and Profile's first-pour state (src/components/profile/ProfileView.tsx:382-387) sit inches from 162 photographs and 1,927 vector glasses the app owns and use none of them.

Thirteen of the 47 are the identical `alert` failure with "Could not load ..." (for example src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx:240-246, src/app/saved.tsx:115), which is the right message but a lot of identical screens.

Because empty titles must be Inter (src/constants/theme.ts:349) and the glyph is bare by design (src/components/ui.tsx:1972-1975), the block never has a picture or a serif. It cannot carry brand voice.
opportunities: Add an optional `art` slot to EmptyState with three skins. (1) `drink`: one featured Dex entry, its photo from drinkPhoto(id) at about 160pt in a 1pt-edged square (decoded at view size), or DrinkArt when it has no photo. Its name goes in Playfair, which Jan allows for drink names, with its #dex number under it. Example: Home empty becomes "Your first pour could be a Negroni". Pick the entry deterministically, such as by day, so it never flickers. (2) `slot`: the Dex's own empty-slot recess (colors.slot and slotDeep with the emboss pair) for collection empties, so they read as an empty display case. (3) `seal`: the mono seal for system and error states.
Keep the glyph-only form for utility lists (Blocked, filters, search) so that rich art means something where it appears. Immersion should go where the drink is the subject.

All three skins are static, so no entrance animation is involved. One image per screen is trivial for the 256MB cache. The art is decorative and hidden from VoiceOver, and the title stays the announced heading.

bland_problems: One ground and one container everywhere. 35 component and screen files set backgroundColor: colors.bg, and 25 sites use the same white Card or ListGroup (src/components/ui.tsx:861-869, 2225-2230). Every screen in this area is cream with white boxes with line edges, and moving between screens changes only the words.

Wine is never a surface. The "one wine thing per view" rule (src/components/ui.tsx:65) has become "wine only as one 48pt button": wineDeep is used only as a pressed state and an edge (src/components/FloatingTabBar.tsx:409), and merlot appears only in the reduced-motion intro. The grain is invisible. Mean luminance change on cream is about 4/255, peaking at 7.5 (Grain.tsx:62 opacity 0.35 times the tile's uniform alpha of 26). Because the noise centres on mid-grey, it mostly greys the page slightly instead of adding paper tooth. The material the file is meant to supply never registers on a phone.
No depth cues at all. No shadow except the tab bar and sheets (src/constants/theme.ts:511-534), no gradient (spec 01 rule 4), and no image grounds. Combined, every element sits on one flat plane.

The brand's ornaments are missing. The brand sheet's gilt hairline rules and small four-point diamond (scripts/icon/brand-sheet.png) appear nowhere. The only divider is a plain 1pt line (src/components/ui.tsx:1034-1051, 2269-2279).

Zero imagery outside the content screens. Of the 162 drink photos, 1,927 DrinkArt glasses, the wax-seal marks and the intro film, none appears in sign-in, the username step, Welcome, Settings, Edit profile, Hold or any of the 47 EmptyState sites. The photos are consumed only by DexCard, the drink page, log, add-drink, CollectionStats and Celebration (src/data/drinkPhotos.ts importers).

The film is the only immersive moment, and the app discards it. It ends on merlot with the seal and dissolves in 280ms to a cream form (VideoIntro.tsx:87). Merlot and wineDeep are never used as fills anywhere after it.

No typographic top end. Every bar title is Inter SemiBold 17 (ScreenTopBar.tsx:124), empty titles are Inter 22 (theme.ts:349), and display 36 is used once (PasswordResetOverlay.tsx:297). Playfair, the speakeasy voice, appears in this area only in the reset overlay's wordmark.

Bare generic glyphs stand in for art: a 28pt `users` on Welcome, a 36pt glyph on every EmptyState, a 40pt `check` on the reset confirmation, and 22pt outline glyphs on all 11 Settings rows. The same `users` glyph heads Welcome, Home's empty feed and Find friends.

Identical stacks with no focal point: five 48pt full-width buttons on sign-in, six identical Cards on Welcome, eleven identical ListRows on Settings, and three stacked 56pt fields on the username step and Edit profile.
Grain that does not register. Its mean change of about 4/255 on cream (Grain.tsx:62) is the only material texture in the app, and it is too faint to be seen on a phone.
The brand outshouted on its own front door. Google's four-colour G and Facebook's #0866FF are the most saturated pixels on the first sign-in screen, while Continue sits at 42% opacity (ui.tsx:2117).

The rules that make it flat are interpretations, not Jan's rules. "One wine thing per view" (ui.tsx:65), "no gradient behind content" and "no image grounds" come from spec 01. Jan's own rules (rectangles with real borders, Instagram structure, the login sheet layout, no caps, Inter chrome with Playfair for the wordmark and drink names) all allow a cellar-wine hero, seal art, drink photos in empty states and a member card.

directions.name: After hours
directions.thesis: Sipply moves from a cream page to a bar after dark. Browsing screens sit on a warm near-black ground (#140E0D). Home and Profile open under a wineDeep "back bar" band lit from above. Cream becomes the paper you write on and read from: sign-in and log sheets, the recipe spec card, the labels on collected Dex cards, and selected chips. Rule of thumb: you look in the dark and write on paper. Two things stop this from reading as dark mode with a wine accent. First, the photos are re-lit, not framed. A deterministic bake (already prototyped, grade.py) turns the grey studio backdrop into a dim tungsten wall that settles to the screen's own ground colour, so every catalog photo glows out of the page with no grey box around it. A locked entry becomes the same shot with the lights off, which takes the collected-vs-locked difference from 8.5/255 to 16/255, with a big saturation drop on top. Second, the collectible system was always light-on-dark material and only now gets its contrast. On cream, taupe was 1.68:1 and the common frame 1.08:1. On night, taupe is 10.2:1, gilt 6.0:1 and giltLit 9.3:1. So rarity finally reads at arm's length: taupe linen, then lit wine, then gilt with a double rule. Playfair moves to display sizes: drink names at 31 on feed photos, 52 on the drink page, 17 on Dex labels and 19 in search. It stays limited to the wordmark and drink names, as Jan's rule says. Everything else keeps Jan's structure: Instagram's layout with none of its identity, rectangles with real 1px edges, no uppercase, and motion only from a visible resting state.

directions.imagery_and_depth:
1. Night grade, a build-time bake that adds no runtime cost. scripts/build-drink-photos.mjs gains a pass:
   - It masks the backdrop (low saturation, mid luminance, highlights allowed only near the glass).
   - It replaces the backdrop with a warm wall: a lerp from night #140E0D to #7C5642 along a Gaussian light pool behind the glass, keeping the stone's own texture.
   - It warms the drink slightly and lets every frame edge settle to #140E0D.
   - Locked becomes 'lights off': 90% desaturated, at 38% exposure, mixed 62% into night.
   - It writes assets/drinks/night/<id>.webp and rebakes locked/. drinkPhoto() returns the night file, and the grey originals are retired, so the number of decoded images and their size do not change.
   - The prototype is /cellar/grade.py (numpy/PIL), and every catalog photo in the mockup is its output.
2. People's photos are never graded. Feed posts, Today's tiles and the profile grid show the photo as taken. A bright daylight photo will be the brightest thing on a night screen, and that is intended: it glows. The only overlays are the nameplate scrim (reelScrimClear → reelScrimMid → 0.86) and the 2–3pt rarity rule along the photo's bottom edge.
3. Depth comes from light and material, not drop shadows:
   - Raised panels are nightRaised with a 1px nightEdge.
   - Paper objects (Dex labels, the spec card, sheets) are the only things that cast shadows on the bar: label 0 2 6 at 0.35, spec card 0 10 30 at 0.45, sheet 0 -8 30 at 0.5. The tab bar keeps its tight lift.
4. Grain stays at 3.5% (the same mid-grey tile), so it reads as a lift on dark. It is mounted per ground, under content, so it stops dusting photos.
5. Vector DrinkArt gets a 'lit' face for collected entries: a radial field from #5A2A22 to night, a counter line at 82% height, a floor shadow, the liquid in its own LIQUID colour, a bone glass outline and a highlight stroke. Locked entries are a debossed impression: the outline in the drink's own liquid hue at 30%, the liquid at 10%, a 1px dark offset and a 10% light offset. Every one of the 1,927 unphotographed entries now carries its own colour instead of one lockInkSoft.
6. Image budget:
   - The Dex grid, Today's tiles, the teaser strip (124x166), the profile shelf (92x100) and Log thumbnails (56) all decode at view size with enforceEarlyResizing and cachePolicy 'disk'.
   - The only large decodes are the feed photo (440x550) and the drink hero (440x500), as now.
   - Feed photos move from 3:4 to 4:5, which saves 37pt per post and about 8% of decode.
   - Fix the two existing breaches before shipping (CollectionStats prize thumbnail, CustomDrinkTile).
directions.motion:
Every motion starts from a fully visible resting state, and nothing uses entering or exiting:
1. Home wordmark condense. scale goes 1 → 0.82 and translateY 0 → -2 as the feed scrolls 0 → 120pt (useAnimatedScrollHandler + interpolate, clamped). If Reanimated stalls, the wordmark stays full size, so nothing can hide. The band is static.
2. Drink-page hero. Keep the existing 0.35 parallax and pull-to-stretch. The 52pt name sits in the scroll content, so it simply rides up over the dissolving hero, with no extra animation.
3. Legendary foil. The existing FoilSweep is retargeted to the paper label's gilt edge on legendary Dex cards only. Its resting position stays off the band, as now.
4. Press feedback:
   - PressableScale 0.97 on Dex cards, Today's tiles, teaser cards, Top-shelf cards and grid tiles.
   - Controls answer with a fill change (night → nightRaised, wine → wineDeep, paper chip → paperSunk).
5. Like.
   - The existing pop stays on the heart, which fills ember.
   - The double-tap burst becomes an ember heart with a 2pt bone outline. It stays unmounted at rest on a JS timer, as now.
6. Optional, gated on a Release-build frame profile: a ±16pt photo parallax inside feed and Dex frames, with the image 8% taller and translate 0 at rest, driven by one shared scroll value rather than a listener per cell.

directions.thesis: Today every surface is cream with 14pt type. Menu card gives each drink its own colour and puts its name at display size, the way a printed cocktail menu or a drinks magazine does. The colour comes from data, not from a theme. At build time the pipeline samples the liquid colour from each of the 162 catalogue photos (and uses liquidColor() for the 1,927 drinks without a photo) and derives four contrast-clamped tokens per drink: seam (a pale backdrop), deep (a colour block that carries bone text at 8.5:1 or better), ink (text-safe on cream) and dmuted. The same pipeline re-bakes each photo's grey studio backdrop toward that drink's seam colour, so a Negroni stands on coral, an Aviation on lavender and a Daiquiri on pale olive. Each screen gets a different dominant ground: a wineDeep cover on Home, a drink-coloured name plate on every post, a multi-coloured Dex grid, an oxblood title band under the Negroni hero, olive for a Daiquiri house pour, a pink cover behind sign-in. There are no gradients-for-mood, glass or glow, and nothing is invented: every colour is measured from the drink. Playfair stays limited to drink names and the wordmark but now runs at 28-68pt. Print devices do the structural work: double rules, dotted recipe leaders, numbered steps, a ruled tally. Collecting finally reads at arm's length, because a collected card is in colour on its seam and a locked one is the drained grey photo on the slot.
