  - Leader: label, dots, value. Draw the dots with react-native-svg Line strokeDasharray measured onLayout, because a single-side dotted border is unreliable on iOS.
  - DexStamp: rectangle, 1pt bone edge.
  - TagOnDark and TagWine: 22pt rectangles.
  - DrinkStage: vector glass on seam with a floor line, cropped viewBox.
  - DrinkPhoto: expo-image wrapper that always passes enforceEarlyResizing, picks graded or locked from collection state, and uses cachePolicy 'disk'.
- EmptyState gets a 'cover' variant (photo plus Playfair headline) for first-run Home.
- ScreenTopBar gets tone and figure props.
- FloatingTabBar: drop the Reels-only condition (FloatingTabBar.tsx:198-200) and add the 2pt indicator.

Pipeline: build-drink-photos.mjs adds the sampling (median OKLCH of saturated pixels, with a less-than-5%-coverage fallback) and the grade pass, then rebuilds locked/ from the original.
risks: The photo grade is a real pipeline change. Re-baking 162 photos changes every catalogue surface at once. Some photos clip or tint glass oddly (window-glare shots like Saturn and Zombie; pale drinks with garnish-dominated samples, e.g. Ramos sampled green before the fallback). Each needs an eyeball pass, and new photos arriving later must go through the same pass. If Jan prefers, briefing the photographer on coloured seamless paper is the higher-quality alternative.

Hue clustering: many classics are red-orange, so Negroni, Clover Club, Paper Plane, Jungle Bird and Boulevardier all derive deep around #6B2011. Two adjacent red posts can still look alike, and that red sits near the brand wine. Possible mitigation: let deep lightness follow the sampled lightness within the contrast band, or pick the sample from the liquid region only.

Contrast on dark: every pair I used passes, measured: dmuted 5.1-5.7:1, bone 8.5-9.1:1 on deeps, giltOnDark 6.0:1 or better, sign-in wordmark 8.0:1 over the real photo pixels. My first draft put giltInk on the slot at 4.41:1; it is fixed to #715619 (5.10:1) and needs adding to check-contrast. The wineSoft seen-tile frame is 3.43:1 (non-text only). Text over users' photos is never used, so no scrim is needed.

Dynamic Type: 36-68pt Playfair names grow huge. Long names ('Three Dots and a Dash', 'Mezcal de Pechuga') need two-line wrapping and a maxFontSizeMultiplier around 1.3 on display roles. Plates must size by content rather than fixed height, and the Dex card plate (fixed 60pt in the mockup) has to grow with text, so card heights in a row need equalising.

First paint on Home: at 4:5 the photo's action row is still under the tab bar on a Pro Max. The fix shown is to name the drink above the photo instead of reclaiming space. Smaller phones show less of the photo.

Instagram structure: putting the author row on a coloured plate with a 36pt drink title is a judgement call. It keeps the structure (author row, photo, actions) but is louder than Instagram's header. Jan should confirm.

Image memory is fine as specified (graded files are the same size; everything decodes at view size). But Stats' prize thumbnail and CustomDrinkTile already break enforceEarlyResizing and must be fixed first. The optional photo parallax must be profiled on a Release build.

Base-spirit chapters need a derived field for the 899 cocktails (first spirit in the recipe) and a mapping of 47 spirit subcategories to families. It is a data-build task with edge cases (split bases, liqueur-led drinks).

Effort: large. Per-drink token generation and checks, the photo re-grade, about 8 new ui.tsx components, a Dex SectionList rewrite, and PostCard, TodaysPours, drink page, Profile, Log and sign-in cover changes. Realistically 2-3 focused weeks plus a device pass. It can ship in slices: tokens and tab bar, then the Dex, then the drink page, then Home.
Rendering caveat: the mockup is HTML with Chrome's font rasteriser and CSS dotted borders. RN line heights for Playfair at 68pt and SVG leaders will differ slightly, so check on device.

directions.name: Cabinet
directions.thesis: Sipply turns into a collector's cabinet with two materials, and collecting a drink moves it from one to the other. The wine lining (wineDeep #3E0A12 with a heavier grain, like baize) is the inside of the cabinet. An empty slot is a recess pressed into that lining: a wine duotone of the drink's own photo with an emboss pass, so it looks blind-stamped. A collected drink is a bone card-stock mount (#FBF8F2) that sits in the slot with a contact shadow, a stamped number plate, a Playfair nameplate and a rarity rule printed on the mount. That rule is a taupe hairline for uncommon, a 2pt wine rule for rare, and a gilt double rule for legendary. Today a collected card differs from a locked one by about 3% in pixels. Here the difference is a change of material that reads at arm's length. The same three-part vocabulary carries every screen. Mounted means it is in your Dex. A loose print means a friend poured it and you have not, which is the Home interleave. A ghost means not yet, in the Dex. The labels look like museum labels on photographs, the recipe like a spec card, and first-poured has a ticket stub. Wine stops being a 2pt accent and becomes a surface: the Home head and the today rail, the Dex tray, the profile top shelf, and the sign-in and log backdrops. Cream stays the reading surface. It avoids looking AI-made in three ways. Nothing is a gradient blob, glass, a pill or a glow. Every object is a bordered rectangle with a job. And the richness comes from Sipply's own data (rarity, Dex numbers, origin, the viewer's local collection) and its own 162 photographs, re-graded warm, not from decoration.
directions.palette_and_grounds: Three grounds, one rule each. (1) PAPER, cream #F7F2EA with a 3.5% grain tile: everything you read, meaning the feed posts, the drink page body, profile header and grid, sheets. (2) LINING, wineDeep #3E0A12 with a stronger grain (the same 128px tile at alpha 20/255, about 8%): the cabinet interior. It covers the Home top bar plus Today rail (0 to 268pt), the Home interleave module, the whole Dex tray under the cabinet front, the Profile top shelf band, the sign-in backdrop and the log collect-preview. A lining band always ends on paper with a 1pt rgba(233,229,223,.14) lip line and a 12pt espresso shadow gradient (.22 to 0), so it reads as a shelf over the page. (3) MAT, bone card stock #FBF8F2: the face of every collected card, the drink label, the spec card, tier plates and mounted prints. Slots: liningDeep #2F070D with inset shadow 0 2 10 rgba(0,0,0,.55) and a bottom highlight rgba(233,229,223,.06). Tab bar: espresso #2B2322 on every tab (the existing Reels skin), 1pt rgba(255,253,249,.12) edge, active reelInk plus a 2pt indicator, rest reelInkDim (5.86:1). Text on lining: onLining #E9E5DF (13.3:1, and 14.5:1 in a slot), onLiningMuted #B8A09B (6.79:1, body-safe), onLiningFaint #A7837F (4.93:1, glyphs and rest states), giltOnLining #C9A458 (7.11:1, the word Legendary). Gilt #B08A3E stays decorative and legendary-only (5.21:1 on lining, 3.02:1 on mat as an edge). Text over photos uses a scrim from rgba(14,11,11,0) to .42 at 42% to .76, plus reelInk and reelTextShadow. Per screen: Home is lining head over paper feed, with a lining interleave every ~6 posts. Dex is a paper cabinet front over the lining tray. The drink page is a full-bleed photo with a mat label over a paper body. Profile is a paper header, a lining top shelf, then a paper grid. Sign-in is a lining backdrop with a paper sheet. Log is a paper page sheet over the dimmed Home head. All new pairs were computed with the WCAG formula, and the ones listed pass.
directions.typography: The two families stay as they are: Playfair Display 600/700 and Inter 400/500/600. No uppercase, and no tracking except the Dex-number stamp. Playfair now reaches display sizes. figure: Playfair Bold 60/60 wine for the Dex count ("38"). display: Playfair Bold 36/42 for the drink-page name. nameplate: Playfair Bold 34/40 reelInk for the drink on a feed photo. wordmark: Playfair Bold 28/34, scaling to 22 when condensed (sign-in uses 44). shelf: Playfair SemiBold 22/28 for Dex shelf headers, the interleave title and the Recipe header. top shelf: Playfair SemiBold 20/26. cardName: Playfair SemiBold 17/21 on a mounted Dex card (was Inter or Playfair 12). rowName: Playfair SemiBold 18/22 in log results. printName: Playfair SemiBold 16/20 on loose prints. tileDrink: Playfair SemiBold 13/17 under Today tiles. A locked card's name drops to Inter Medium 14 onLiningMuted, so the type change is part of the collect moment. Inter: caption prose 15/22 (was 14), username 14 SemiBold, meta 13/18, tier word and plate 12/16 Medium, dexNumber stamp 11/18 Medium with 1.2pt tracking and tabular figures, drawn inside a 20pt radius-4 plate with a 1pt taupe edge (taupeInk 5.55:1 on mat). Recipe amounts are Inter SemiBold 17 tabular in wine, metric in 12 muted beneath, the ingredient in 16 ink. Bar titles stay Inter SemiBold 17/20. Rarity is always said in words beside its mark: ring for common, filled dot for uncommon and rare, gilt sparkle for legendary. Overlays on media cap maxFontSizeMultiplier at 1.3, as overlays do today.
directions.imagery_and_depth: Photography: scripts/build-drink-photos.mjs bakes two new variants per catalog photo, the same way it already bakes /locked. (a) warm/: a luminance-weighted warm multiply (1.02, .955, .875) on the mid-highlights, colour 1.22, contrast 1.06. The cold #C5C6C5 seamless becomes a parchment that sits on cream, and these files are used for collected cards, heroes, tiles and fallbacks. (b) ghost/: a luminance map into wine duotone (#26050B to #6C2A35) plus a 0.8px-blurred EMBOSS pass, used for locked photographed slots. It replaces /locked, whose 8.5/255 drain was invisible. Both are baked at 512 to 900px, with no runtime filters. The prototype bake is in tools/bake.py. Drinks with no photo (1,927): collected cards get a lit back-bar window (merlot to #4A0D16 for cocktails, #4A3B38 to espresso for spirits) with a counter band over the bottom 23% and a 1pt highlight line. The glass stands on it in full LIQUID colour with a soft contact shadow. Locked vector slots draw the same glass as a blind stamp: a 1.4pt rgba(233,229,223,.24) outline over a 1pt-down black outline, and the drink's own liquid hue at 22%. Depth has exactly three layers. The seat shadow is new and only for a mat resting on lining: 0 1 0 rgba(14,11,11,.45), 0 8 18 rgba(14,11,11,.34). The recess is the inset shadow on slots. Floating keeps the existing tab-bar and sheet shadows, plus the drink label riding over the hero (0 12 28 rgba(43,35,34,.16)). Cards on paper still cast no shadow. Grain goes on grounds only, never over photographs (per-ground tiles grain-paper and grain-lining replace the global overlay). Image budget: Dex windows 171x140pt decode to about 513x420px, about 0.9MB each, so about 30 mounted cells at windowSize 5 come to about 27MB. Today tiles at 74x98pt are tiny. One 440x550 feed photo per cell at view size. Ghost files are 512px. Everything uses enforceEarlyResizing and cachePolicy 'disk', as DexCard does. The Stats prize thumbnail and CustomDrinkTile breaches are fixed first.
directions.motion: Every motion starts from the fully visible resting state, so a stalled Reanimated worklet leaves the finished layout. No entering or exiting animations, and check-design stays as it is. (1) Home wordmark condense is scroll-linked: scale 1 to 0.79 (28 to 22pt) and the bar's lip line opacity 0 to 1 over the first 160pt of scroll, using useAnimatedScrollHandler plus interpolate with clamp. The rail scrolls away natively. (2) Dex cabinet front collapse is scroll-linked: the 60pt figure translates and scales into the bar title as "38 of 2,089", while the tier plates scroll natively. (3) Sticky shelf headers come from SectionList stickySectionHeadersEnabled, which is native, not an animation. (4) Press: PressableScale 0.97 on cards, tiles and prints, and the seat shadow's opacity deepens .34 to .5 while pressed. (5) FoilSweep (existing, DexCard.tsx:134) is retargeted to the gilt double rule and the legendary plate. It runs once when a legendary card becomes viewable, never loops, sits off-band at rest, and is off under Reduce Motion. (6) Drink hero parallax and pull-to-stretch stay as now, since they are transforms from 0. (7) Optional feed photo parallax: the image is 8% taller than its frame and translates within ±12pt from one shared scroll value. Translate 0 is the rest state. Ship only after a Release-build frame profile. (8) The collect moment (CelebrationOverlay) shows the mounted card in its final state at once. The number plate then does a one-shot press-in (scale 1.12 to 1 on the plate only), with one foil pass for legendary and a success haptic. If either stalls, the card is already complete. (9) The like pop stays. The double-tap burst becomes a wine-filled heart with a 2pt bone outline, still mounted and unmounted by a JS timer. (10) Pull to refresh gets tintColor wine on paper and onLining on the lining head.

per_screen.change: The top bar and Today rail sit on one lining band (0 to 268pt) with a light status bar, a bone wordmark and bone glyphs, and a bone activity dot with a 2pt lining ring. The rail tiles become mounted prints: 80x104 bone mat 3pt, photo inside. Unseen tiles get a 2pt lining gap plus a 2pt bone outer ring. Seen tiles get a dull #6B3A41 mat and muted labels. Two label lines: username Inter 12, then the drink in Playfair 13, so the row says what was poured. Your own tile shows your latest pour, or your last logged drink's catalog photo, with a 24pt bone plate and a wine plus, replacing the grey action box. The rail ends in a lip line and a 12pt shadow. The bar's wordmark condenses on scroll. The feed photo goes to 4:5 (440x550) so the nameplate clears the tab bar on first paint. A Find friends tile appears only when nobody you follow has poured. Pull to refresh is tinted. Posts are separated by a 12pt sunk page gap with 1pt line edges. A footer in Sipply's own words, 'That's every pour from the last 7 days' with a Log a pour button, closes the feed.

The header drops to avatar, username and time. The drink moves onto the photo as a museum-label nameplate: a scrim with plates for the #dex number, the tier (gilt edge and sparkle for legendary, wineSoft edge for rare) and the viewer's Dex status ('In your Dex' with a check, or 'New to your Dex' with a plus via useIsUnlocked, tapping through to /drink/[id]). The name is Playfair Bold 34, with subcategory, glass and origin in Inter 14 beneath. Rare and legendary posts get a full-bleed 2pt wineSoft or 3pt gilt rule along the photo's bottom edge. The VoiceOver order is the visible header, then a single nameplate label. A post without a photo falls back to drinkPhoto(id) warm, then the lit back-bar vector, never a pink square. The caption goes to 15/22 and the action row is unchanged.

'Not in your Dex yet' on lining (Playfair 22 title, Inter 13 subtitle), followed by a horizontal row of loose prints. Each print is 136x164, unmounted with a 1pt bone edge, showing the friend's photo or a catalog fallback, the drink in Playfair 16, then the tier word and the friend's username. Built only from the feed store plus useIsUnlocked, so no proof is invented.

The paper cabinet front replaces the 2pt rule, the sentence and the Settings-style My Bar row. It holds the Playfair 60 wine count with 'in your Dex / of 2,089 · 1.8%', a static strip of the last three caught cards as 32x42 mounts (a gilt edge if legendary), and four tier plates (Common 21 of 619, Uncommon 11 of 595, Rare 5 of 646, Legendary 1 of 229, the legendary plate gilt-edged on giltWash). Then the search field and filter chips (radius 8, 1pt edges). My Bar moves to a bottle glyph in the bar's left slot. Below that the tray is lining: a SectionList by subcategory with sticky Playfair 22 shelf headers, an 'n of N collected' count and a 2pt bone progress line, plus a ledge between card rows. Cards are 199pt wide: mounted with the tier rule, plate and Playfair 17 name if collected, or a recess with a ghost photo or blind-stamped glass, Inter muted name and lock if not. Locked legendary slots get a gilt hairline and a gilt tier word, so collectors can see what is worth hunting. The figure collapses into the bar on scroll.

The hero is a warm-graded photo, or for the 92% without one a lit back-bar stage with the glass at about 60% width. 40pt controls with a dark translucent fill sit over it. A mat label card rides 40pt up over the hero: the tier's rule (gilt double rule for legendary), a plate row (#0009, the tier word, 'In your Dex'), the name in Playfair 36, a bottle-label facts row (Origin / Glass / Strength with hairline dividers), and a perforated ticket stub reading 'First poured 12 Sep · 3 pours · Your photos'. Recipe is a mat spec card with amounts first in a fixed 86pt column (Inter SemiBold 17 tabular wine, metric beneath) and the ingredient after. Steps take Playfair numerals. Bar trivia becomes a pull-quote band on lining. A pinned 48pt 'Log another pour' (or 'Log this drink') dock replaces both the mid-page locked card and the end button. Locked entries show 'Not in your Dex yet' in the plate row.

The header stays to Instagram's structure (86pt avatar, name, posts/followers/following, bio, Edit profile / Share profile / find-friends, all 1pt-bordered rectangles), keeping the current rule of no Dex count in the header. New: a lining 'Top shelf' band showing the three rarest drinks in this person's posts as small mounted cards, Playfair 14 names, the tier in words. It is built from public posts, so it works on peers too, because the collection itself never leaves the owner's phone. On your own profile it carries a 'Dex 38' link. A text TabStrip (Posts / Reels / Dex) with a 2pt ink indicator sits under the band's lip. In the grid, legendary pour tiles get a reelScrim marker with a gilt sparkle and a 3pt gilt bottom rule.

Jan's layout is kept exactly: a 56pt title bar (close, 'Log in or sign up'), the grouped Country or region / Phone number box with a 1pt lineControl edge, helper text, a full-width wine Continue, the 'or' divider, then four stacked outlined provider buttons with leading icons, and the consent line. Added immersion lives only behind the sheet: the lining cabinet with the Playfair 44 bone wordmark, '2,089 drinks. Start your Dex with the next one.', and three mounted cards (common, legendary raised 14pt, uncommon) whose tops show above the sheet edge at y=304.

A page sheet over the dimmed Home head. Your photo appears as a 90x120 mounted print with Retake / Choose another as 36pt bordered buttons. 'What was it?' with the search field. Results sit in one white list with 1pt edges. Each 72pt row has a 44x56 mounted thumbnail (warm catalog photo, or a lit vector glass for unphotographed drinks), the name in Playfair 18, and '#0127 · Spirit-Forward · Common' with the tier word in its colour. On the right is the Dex status, either a wine 'New' tag or a muted 'In your Dex' with a check. The selected row is wineWash with a 1.5pt wine edge and 'New to your Dex'. Before saving, a lining preview strip shows the collect moment in its final state: 'Negroni joins your Dex', with 'Card 39 of 2,089 · #0127 · Common' and the mounted mini card. Then Save to Dex (secondary) and Save & post (wine). The Note field stays below the results, as today.

The espresso tab bar on every tab gets a 2pt indicator above the active slot, active reelInk and rest reelInkDim, and the wine plus box gets a 1pt bone edge. That is a one-condition change at FloatingTabBar.tsx:198-200. ScreenTopBar gains tone: 'paper' | 'lining' (bone glyphs and title, light status bar, lining lip line) and an optional subtitle.

Effort is large. The work: tokens and contrast pairs, the DexMount family, a DexCard rewrite, a Dex FlatList to SectionList change (with a getItemLayout redo), the PostCard nameplate, the Home lining head, the interleave module, the profile top shelf, the drink label, spec card and pinned dock, two pipeline bakes, ScreenTopBar tone and the tab bar skin. Copy and metaphor. The visual metaphor is 'cabinet', but the copy keeps 'Dex' everywhere ('In your Dex', 'New to your Dex'), so the brand noun does not split. 'Top shelf' and 'Not in your Dex yet' are new strings to confirm with Jan. 'First poured 12 Sep · 3 pours' needs the local collection's first-log date and pour count, which exist on-device only.

scores.verdict: This is the most immersive of the three in the screenshots. The drink page (the re-lit hero fades into the dark, the 52pt name rides up over it, then the paper spec card) and the Dex (lights-off locked cards against lit cards with paper labels, and the gilt legendary frame) are the best single frames across all three directions. It also follows Jan's rules most strictly: Playfair only on drink names and the wordmark, Inter avatar initials, rounded rectangles with 1px edges, and the sign-in sheet exactly as specified. The weaknesses: it trades cream monotony for night monotony, since all seven frames share one dark mood. It demotes the brand's bone cream ground to 'paper'. The band relies on a radial amber glow, which is a mood gradient and a known AI tell. People's ungraded grey studio photos glare on Home at rest and in the Profile grid. It is also the biggest build: a Tone context, 19 route grounds and a heuristic-mask bake that needs a visual check of every photo.

This is the least bland and least AI-looking direction. Colour measured from each drink, 36-68pt Playfair names, double rules, dotted recipe leaders, the ruled rarity tally and the 'Florence, Italy, 1919' dateline make it feel like a printed menu, and every screen and every post looks different. The Negroni drink page and the pink sign-in cover are lovely. The problems: the navy, olive and brown plates pull the app away from wine-and-gilt Porcelain Speakeasy, so Sipply stops having one colour. The colour plate with a 36pt title on every author row is louder than Instagram's header and bends the structure Jan asked for. Inactive tabs lose their text labels. Avatar initials are set in Playfair. The Log mockup drops the photo step. The build needs heavy new machinery: per-drink tokens with contrast checks, the grade pass, SVG leaders measured onLayout, and base-spirit chapters derived for 899 cocktails. Similar red drinks also cluster around one deep red, close to brand wine.

Winner, narrowly. The bone mount sitting in a wine recess turns collecting itself into the visual system. Collected and locked cards now read at arm's length as different materials, where today they differ by about 3%. Wine becomes a surface (the Home head, the Dex tray, Top shelf, the sign-in cabinet, the 'Negroni joins your Dex' preview in Log) instead of a 2pt accent. It stays inside the Porcelain Speakeasy palette with cream as the reading ground, and it is the most incremental build because it keeps the paper tokens and adds two bakes the way /locked already works. Weak spots: the 'warm' bake still reads as beige studio photography, the drink page and profile grid look close to today's, and Playfair has spread into headings, figures and avatar initials, which breaks Jan's typography rule. All of these can be fixed by borrowing from the other two directions.

scores.verdict: The most atmospheric of the three. The re-lit catalog photos on the Dex and drink page are great, and the drink page (a hero that dissolves into the ground, a 4-column label band, a paper spec card, a pinned 'Log another Hanky Panky') is the best single screen in any direction. It is also the riskiest to ship this week. It turns the whole app dark through a Tone context in about 10 primitives and 19 route grounds. Every screen not in the mockup (settings, activity, stats, empty and error states, native page sheets, keyboard appearance, alerts, RefreshControl, splash and status bar) flips with it, so the regression surface is the largest. Its photo bake uses a heuristic mask and replaces the originals, so a bad bake ships everywhere. The colour system has traps it admits to: the wine fill is 1.4:1 on night and needs an edge everywhere, and wineLit and nightInkMuted fail over media, so someone has to police them. The mockup breaks its own plaque rule on the teaser cards. People's photos stay ungraded, so on Home at rest and the Profile grid the brightest thing on a night screen is a grey studio wall, which undercuts the mood. Bone cream drops from the ground to sheets only, so the 'Porcelain' brand reads as a dark theme. Every screen is night plus a wine band, so there is little variety between them.

Best answer to 'monotonous'. Colour comes from each drink's own data, so the feed changes hue post by post, the Dex is multicoloured, and every drink page and profile looks different. The print devices (double rules, amount-first recipe rows with dotted leaders, a ruled rarity tally, an origin-and-year dateline) give it real character. Engineering is sound in principle: the per-drink tokens are a generated table checked in check-contrast.mjs, colour blocks are plain Views with no image memory, and paper stays the default ground, so there is no app-wide theme flip. The costs: about 8 new components; SVG dotted leaders measured onLayout in every list row; a base-spirit chapter field to derive for 899 cocktails; a saturation-mask regrade of every photo; and hue clustering, where Negroni, Clover Club and Boulevardier all land near #6B2011, next to brand wine. Two problems are visible in the frames. Resting tab-bar slots lose their text labels (only the active tab is labelled), which is a legibility regression. The post's author row moves inside a 36pt coloured drink plate, which bends Instagram's post structure. Navy, olive and lavender grounds dilute wine and gilt as the brand. The flat vector glasses (Mezcal de Pechuga feature cell, Log thumbnails) read as clip art next to the photos.

Winner for a ship-this-week engineer. It keeps Jan's brand exactly: cream stays the reading ground, wineDeep becomes a grained lining surface, and gilt stays legendary-only. Collecting finally reads at arm's length as a change of material: a bone mount with a seat shadow versus a wine-duotone embossed ghost slot. The same mount, loose-print and ghost vocabulary carries Home, Dex, Profile, sign-in and Log. Risk is low because paper stays the default. Lining is a handful of band and tray components rather than an app-wide Tone switch, so the unmocked screens are not touched. Its photo bake is a global warm multiply plus a duotone-and-emboss ghost, with no per-photo masking heuristics to QA. Text mostly sits on measured cream or lining pairs. Seat shadows and inset slot shadows map to RN boxShadow on the new architecture, which Reanimated 4 already needs. Every motion is scroll-linked or starts at rest, and no mockup uses keyframes or opacity 0. Weaknesses: the drink page is mostly paper and the least immersive of the three. Home at rest is still dominated by a grey user photo. Every screen is the same wine-and-cream two-tone, so screens vary by layout, not palette. The Profile mockup drops the 'in Dex' count. Locked vector slots (Sloe Gin Fizz) are so faint they read as empty cells.
